Mush  <jlt14@columbia.edu> wrote:
>if a political cards says +1 stealth, is the political action at +1 or 
>does the vampire?  how does the whole "political phase" work?  

Basic procedure to a political action:

1.  Vampire takes a political action.  Typically this action is provided
	by a card in hand, such as Disputed Territory, but occasionally is
	provided by a card in play, such as burning Anarch Revolt.
2.  This action may be blocked as normal.  I believe all political cards
	played from hand are at +1 stealth; cards in play will tell you if
	the action they provide is at stealth, but again, probably most
	of them say this.
3.  If action is blocked, then combat ensues as normal.  If it is not
	blocked, then the terms of the vote are set; these are sometimes
	obvious, as with Anarch Revolt, but sometimes you have choices, such
	as they two that Disputed Territory gives you.
4.  The vote proceeds.  All players cast votes, which they get from titled
	vampires, from action modifiers and reactions, from cards in play,
	from trading in the edge, from burning political cards in hand, etc.
	If the vote was started by a political action in hand, then the acting
	player gets one vote from that card.  If a card in play was used to
	call the vote, then the player typically does not get a free vote
	in this manner.
